q: As per PEC and NEC, receptacles shall be installed such that no point measured horizontally along the floor line of any wall space is more than how many meters from a receptacle outlet?
n: Receptacles must be placed so no point along the floor line of a wall space is more than 1.80 m (6 ft) from an outlet. Source: PEC 2017 / NEC, Art. 2.10.52(A)(1).

q: In a building's internal telecommunications infrastructure, a PABX is installed to manage call routing between internal extensions and the public network. In telecommunications engineering terminology, what does PABX stand for?
n: PABX stands for Private Automatic Branch Exchange. It routes calls between internal extensions and the public network. Source: ITU-T telecommunications terminology; Stein & Reynolds, MEEB (telephone systems).

q: In building ICT and structured cabling design, each floor or zone of a facility typically contains a dedicated room that houses patch panels, switches, fiber termination points, and horizontal cabling distribution. This room connects to the building's main distribution frame through backbone cabling. What does the acronym IDF stand for?
n: IDF stands for Intermediate Distribution Frame, the floor or zone telecom room linked to the MDF by backbone cabling. Source: ANSI/TIA-569 and TIA-568 (telecommunications spaces).

q: In structured cabling and building ICT design, the central room that houses core network equipment, backbone termination, servers, and the primary distribution point for all telecommunications systems is typically located on the ground floor or a dedicated equipment level. This room connects to all IDFs throughout the building. What does the acronym MDF stand for?
n: MDF stands for Main Distribution Frame, the central room for core network equipment and backbone termination. Source: ANSI/TIA-569 and TIA-568.

q: In large buildings such as airports, malls, hospitals, and high-rise towers, a specialized system is often installed to improve indoor cellular coverage by distributing radio signals through antennas, repeaters, and structured cabling. This system ensures reliable mobile communication even in areas where external signals are weak. What does the acronym DAS stand for?
n: DAS stands for Distributed Antenna System. It spreads cellular signals indoors through antennas, repeaters and cabling. Source: NFPA 1221 / IFC 510 (in-building radio coverage); TIA-5054.

q: In modern commercial installations, the most widely used twisted-pair copper cable for data transmission—commonly deployed to support network speeds of up to 10 Gbps in short-to-medium-length runs—is
n: Category 6 is the most widely used commercial data cable. It supports 10 Gbps on shorter runs (up to about 55 m). Source: ANSI/TIA-568.2-D.

q: Which connector is typically used for analog telephone lines in residential and commercial installations?
n: Analog telephone lines use the RJ-11 connector. RJ-45 is for data. Source: ANSI/TIA-968 (telephone connectors).

q: Ceiling used to conceal utilities
n: A dropped (suspended) ceiling hangs below the structure and hides ducts, pipes and wiring in the plenum above. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (Suspended Ceilings).

q: If the client is into green materials, which will you use for the flooring?
n: Linoleum is made from natural, renewable materials (linseed oil, wood flour, cork, jute) and is biodegradable. That makes it the green choice here. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (resilient flooring); USGBC LEED material credits.

q: Which of the following area of the house is most suitable for rubber flooring?
n: Rubber flooring is resilient, cushioned and slip-resistant, which suits a children's playroom. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (resilient flooring).

q: Which flooring has pigments throughout the thickness of the material and NOT only on the surface?
n: Homogeneous vinyl has its pattern and pigment through its full thickness, so it does not wear off as surface prints do. Source: EN ISO 10581 (homogeneous PVC floor coverings).

q: From among the choices, which material absorbs sound the best?
n: Acoustic board (fibrous or perforated panels) is built to absorb sound. It has a much higher NRC than gypsum, plywood or fiber-cement board. Source: Egan, Architectural Acoustics; Long, Architectural Acoustics (sound absorption coefficients).

q: A commercial gym installs a new heavy-duty treadmill on a reinforced concrete slab. During operation, the equipment causes noticeable structure-borne vibration that can be felt in the office spaces below. To reduce the transmission of vibration through the concrete structure, what acoustic treatment should be used?
o: Neoprene or rubber vibration isolation pads
n: Resilient neoprene or rubber isolation pads decouple vibrating equipment from the slab and cut structure-borne vibration. Source: ASHRAE Handbook—HVAC Applications, Ch. 49 (vibration isolation); Egan, Architectural Acoustics; Long, Architectural Acoustics.

q: Which of the following provides the most effective functional solution for reducing structural floor vibrations in a building?
n: A floating floor rests on resilient isolators above the structural slab. It decouples the surface and reduces vibration and impact transmission. Source: Egan, Architectural Acoustics; Long, Architectural Acoustics (floating floors).

q: A client hires you 10 design a home recording studio where both vocal and instrumental tracks will be recorded. The room is adjacent to a bedroom, and the client specifically wants maximum sound isolation, not just interior acoustic treatment. Considering real-world studio construction standards. which wall assembly provides the most effective isolation for this application?
o: Single stud wall with fiberglass insulation and acoustic foam panels
Lightweight metal stud wall with decorative acoustic panels
Hollow block wall with a single layer of gypsum board
Decoupled double-stud wall with mineral wool insulation, multiple gypsum layers, and damping compound
n: Decoupled double-stud walls with mineral wool, multiple gypsum layers and damping compound combine mass, decoupling, absorption and damping. They give the highest isolation for studios. Source: Egan, Architectural Acoustics; Long, Architectural Acoustics (STC of wall assemblies).

q: A client wants a home recording studio but refuses any construction work. Only surface-applied materials are allowed on the existing 4" CHB wall. Which option gives the best improvement in recording quality under these limitations?
o: Thick broadband acoustic panels (mineral wool or fiberglass)
n: Surface treatment cannot add isolation, but thick broadband absorbers (mineral wool or fiberglass) improve the room's recording acoustics most. Paint, wallpaper and thin foam do little. Source: Egan, Architectural Acoustics; Long, Architectural Acoustics (absorption vs. isolation).

q: A law firm is constructing a confidential conference room where speech privacy is critical. The walls are designed to achieve STC 55, and the mechanical system is already acoustically treated. During commissioning, the consultant notes that the door assembly is now the weakest point in the enclosure, allowing intelligible speech to leak into the corridor. To match the acoustic performance of the wall and minimize sound transmission, which door type should be installed?
o: PVC flush door with decorative laminate
Hollow metal door with standard perimeter gaps
Double-glazed glass panel door with laminate
n: Of these doors, a heavy solid-core wood door, preferably gasketed, comes closest to the wall's STC. Hollow, light or glazed doors with gaps leak sound. Source: Egan, Architectural Acoustics; Long, Architectural Acoustics (door STC ratings).

q: A client is converting a spare room into a dedicated home theater. The goal is to achieve smooth bass response, minimal standing waves, and predictable speaker placement for a 7.1 surround system. The ceiling height is fixed, and no structural changes can be made. Given these constraints, which room proportion provides the most acoustically stable geometry and avoids modal overlap?
o: Nearly square room with similar length and width
n: A rectangular room longer than it is wide spreads out the room modes. Square plans stack modes and give uneven bass. Source: Everest, Master Handbook of Acoustics (room proportions).

q: Which room proportion is considered ideal for acoustics. minimizing standing waves and preventing resonant frequency buildup?
n: Unequal dimensions (e.g., Bolt or golden-ratio proportions) spread the resonant modes. Cubes and squares make them coincide. Source: Everest, Master Handbook of Acoustics.

q: For optimum sound isolation
n: For sound isolation, a partition should be heavy (mass law) and limp, with low stiffness, to avoid coincidence and resonance. Source: Egan, Architectural Acoustics; Long, Architectural Acoustics (mass law; coincidence effect).

q: Where do you place the acoustic panel boards if the space is narrow?
n: In a narrow room the closely spaced parallel walls cause flutter echoes, so absorptive panels work best on the walls. Source: Egan, Architectural Acoustics (flutter echo control).

q: Which ceiling treatment provides the best overall acoustic performance, effectively controlling both reflections and reverberation within a room?
n: Combining diffusive and absorptive materials controls both strong reflections and reverberation while keeping the room lively. Source: Egan, Architectural Acoustics; Cox & D'Antonio, Acoustic Absorbers and Diffusers.

q: Best orientation for solar panels
n: In the northern hemisphere (including the Philippines), solar panels should face south for the most sun. Source: NREL, PV system orientation guidance; DOE-Philippines solar rooftop guidelines.

q: Collects rain from roofs, etc.
n: A storm drain collects rainwater from roofs and paved areas. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 11 (Storm Drainage).

q: Which of the following factors, though seemingly significant, is not considered in the determination of gutter sizes?
n: Gutters are sized from rainfall intensity and roof area (pitch adjusts the effective area). Wind speed is not used. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 11 (sizing of gutters and leaders).

q: You are assessing roof-edge drainage components for a structure experiencing perimeter soil erosion and moisture intrusion due to uncontrolled roof runoff. To prevent further damage, which element is primarily responsible for capturing roof water along the eaves and conveying it toward the downspout system for controlled discharge away from the foundation?
n: Roof gutters collect water along the eaves and carry it to downspouts, discharging it away from the foundation. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 11; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Which drainage component is specifically designed to collect, filter debris, and redirect floodwater into an underground stormwater system, preventing surface accumulation and localized flooding?
n: A catch basin collects surface runoff, traps debris and sediment, and sends the water into the underground storm system. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 11; Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: Collects waste water
n: The house (building) drain collects wastewater from the soil and waste stacks inside the building and carries it to the house sewer. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Definitions (Building Drain).

q: Required when there is no public sewer system
n: A septic tank is needed where no public sewer is available. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 11 / Appendix (Private Sewage Disposal); PD 856, Ch. XVII.

q: Drainage system that includes black, gray and storm water
n: A combined house (building) drain can carry black water, gray water and storm water. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Definitions (Building Drain, combined).

q: Why are storm drainage systems generally separated from sanitary sewer systems in modern building design?
o: To prevent excessive stormwater from overwhelming sewage conveyance and treatment facilities
To increase the pressure available in the sanitary drainage system
To allow wastewater to discharge directly into natural waterways
To reduce the number of drainage pipes required within the building
n: Storm water is kept out of the sanitary sewer so heavy runoff does not overload sewers and treatment plants. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 11; Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: A vent connecting one or more individual vents with a vent stack or stack vent is called a
n: A branch vent connects one or more individual vents with a vent stack or stack vent. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Sec. 2 (Definitions – Vent, Branch).

q: A pipe installed to vent a single fixture trap, connecting with the vent system above the fixture served or terminating in the open air, is called a/an
n: An individual (back) vent is a pipe installed to vent a single fixture trap. It connects with the vent system above the fixture served or terminates outdoors. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Sec. 2 (Definitions – Vent, Individual).

q: A branch vent that serves two or more traps and extends from in front of the last fixture connection of a horizontal branch to the vent stack is called a
n: A circuit vent is a branch vent that serves two or more traps. It extends from in front of the last fixture connection of a horizontal branch to the vent stack. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Sec. 2 (Definitions – Vent, Circuit).

q: A vent connecting at the junction of two fixture drains and serving as a vent for both fixtures is called a
n: A common (unit) vent is a vent connecting at the junction of two fixture drains and serving as a vent for both fixtures. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Sec. 2 (Definitions – Vent, Common).

q: A vertical vent pipe installed primarily to provide circulation of air to and from any part of the drainage system is called a
n: A vent stack is a vertical vent pipe installed mainly to circulate air to and from any part of the drainage system. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Sec. 2 (Definitions – Vent Stack).

q: Which type of vent is directly connected to the trap arm of a single plumbing fixture to prevent siphonage and maintain proper air circulation?
n: An individual (back) vent connects to the trap arm of a single fixture. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 9 (Vents).

q: In a multi-storey plumbing system, what do you call the portion of a soil or waste stack that extends vertically above the highest fixture and continues through the roof to provide venting?
n: The stack vent is the part of a soil or waste stack above the highest fixture branch, extending through the roof. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Definitions (Stack Vent).

q: What type of vent is typically used to serve two plumbing fixtures located on opposite sides of the same wall, allowing both to discharge into a shared horizontal branch while maintaining proper air circulation?
n: A common vent serves two fixtures on opposite sides of a wall that connect at the same level. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 9 (Common Vents).

q: Which device is designed to intercept fats, oils and grease (FOG) from kitchen wastewater before it enters the sanitary sewer by using gravity and a baffle system?
n: A grease interceptor (grease trap) uses gravity separation and baffles to hold back fats, oils and grease from kitchen wastewater before the wastewater reaches the sanitary sewer. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Sec. 1011 (Grease Traps and Interceptors).
